newsitem.title: USA: KeyCorp sells 35 branches to ALBANK.
newsitem.headline: KeyCorp sells 35 branches to ALBANK.

text.p: KeyCorp said it has reached a definitive agreement to sell 35 of its branches in New York State to ALBANK Financial Corp.

As of October 31, the 35 branches had total deposits of about $530 million, loans of $53 million and employed 200 people. The agreement calls for ALBANK to pay a premium equal to about seven percent on average deposit balances measured just prior to closing, which is expected near the end of the second quarter of 1997, subject to regulatory approvals and various other conditions.
As part of the deal, ALBANK has an option to include certain small business, consumer, and mortgage loans related to the branches, along with deposits.
In November, KeyCorp announced its intention to sell 140 and consolidate an additional 140 of its 1,218 KeyCenters in 1997 in conjunction with the transformation of its U.S. retail office network.

KeyCorp also said it has identified and completed the customer notification process for 109 of the branches that it will consolidate this year across its franchise -- about 80 percent of the total to be consolidated. Following completion of the sale to ALBANK and consolidations, KeyBank will operate some 265 offices in the State of New York.
